## The idea

A Director of IT Service Operations & Excellence at a multi-state blood services organization
needs to be credible in four directions at once: with FDA, with AABB, with the CIO, and with
the Quality Analyst who reports to him. That takes more than one course. It takes enough of the
blood-banking, regulatory, and quality-systems world to ask the right question and catch a
wrong answer — without trying to become the Quality Analyst's job.

## Six things this curriculum builds

1. **How a blood center actually works** — donor to hospital, and where IT sits in that
   pipeline.
2. **How to read the regulatory landscape** — telling an FDA regulation, FDA guidance, AABB
   standard, and industry practice apart, and knowing which one is binding.
3. **Quality systems** — deviations, CAPA, change control, document control, audits: the AABB
   Quality System Essentials, in practice.
4. **Validation and BECS** — reading a validation package, Part 11, and data integrity (ALCOA+)
   for electronic records.
5. **Security, privacy, and vendor oversight** — where HIPAA and FDA expectations overlap, and
   what a BECS vendor's change notice obligates you to do.
6. **The ITSM bridge and directing the Quality Analyst** — translating ITIL practice into
   AABB/FDA language for the CIO, and reviewing a direct report's work well enough to catch what
   an inspector would catch.

## Tracks

| Track | Courses |
|---|---|
| Foundations | Reading a CFR citation · The regulatory landscape |
| 1. Blood Center Operations | Blood center operations, donor to hospital |
| 2. Quality Systems & Compliance | Quality system essentials · FDA & AABB in practice |
| 3. Validation, BECS & Data Integrity | CSV & BECS · Data integrity & records |
| 4. Security, Privacy & Vendors | Security, privacy & vendor oversight |
| 5. ITSM Bridge | ITSM for regulated blood services *(capstone)* |
| 6. Directing the Quality Analyst | Directing the Quality Analyst |

## Recommended order — first six months

Sequenced for what matters most, first: understand the business, then run the quality systems
and direct the Quality Analyst, then go deep on validation and BECS, then round out security,
vendors, and the capstone that ties it back to the CIO.

1. Foundations (regulatory landscape orientation)
2. Blood center operations
3. Quality system essentials
4. Directing the Quality Analyst
5. CSV & BECS
6. Data integrity & records
7. FDA & AABB in practice (inspection readiness)
8. Security, privacy & vendor oversight
9. ITSM for regulated blood services *(capstone)*

## How courses appear here

Courses show up in the sidebar under **Courses** as they're built — one module at a time, one
module per work session. Nothing here is built yet; this page describes the plan.
